chapter: The Footlight Club and Washington friends
title: Count Basie's band arrives; meeting Lester Young and the Paul Jones story
summary: Basie's new sound reaches the Howard Theatre and Lester Young, a friend of Phil Phillips, becomes Malachi's acquaintance.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Going back a little bit, around 1936, all of a sudden

this new band jumped into popularity. Everybody was listening to Jimmy Lunceford and Duke Ellington and Fletcher Henderson, Chick Webb, Earl Hines -- these were the major bands. All of a sudden, this band came with this number that was called "One O'Clock Jump." And it was a band called Count Basie. So everybody said, "Here comes another band. There's Duke Ellington, Cab Calloway -- here comes some guy who's a count." But then when you began to listen to the band, it had something different about it in every kind of way. There were no bands that were sounding like that. And all of the bands that came through here... They had bands like McKinney's Cotton Pickers... Every major band that you can think of came through here. But Basie had this different kind of a sound.

I'll never forget the time that they first came to the Howard Theatre. The bus used to stop right there on T Street and unload the musicians, and they'd go find their respective hotels or rooms or whatever. Most of the guys would wind up going in this place, you know. So it happens that the tenor saxophone player with the Basie band, Lester Young, had been long, lifetime friends with Leonard Phillips. I don't know whether Otto Jones was in that particular thing or not... Yeah, yes he was. So anyway, I got to meet Lester Young through them.
And of course, there was another hook-up that I

understand happened when I just happened not to be on the scene -- Lester Young's thing with Paul Jones. I got stories about it... Always stories like that are conflicting, you know. Naturally, Phil and Otto, being from out West and everything, and having a different feeling about things... Phil could give you the impression that Lester had walked in and walked all over top of Paul, you know. Well, I wasn't there, so I can't say. But I know that Paul was an excellent saxophone player, and there's no question about Lester Young. Nevertheless, this is just one of those incidents that happened.
